title: Decompose a Hard Problem with TRIZ-Inspired Contradictions
subtitle: Expose the conflict before optimizing around it.
description: Describe the unwanted result, expose the trade-off or contradiction, split the system into parts, and check a change that removes a constraint instead of merely optimizing around it.

lifeOsSource.hack: When a problem resists ordinary optimization, write the contradiction explicitly and look for a way to separate the conflicting requirements by time, place, condition, component, or role.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: State the unwanted outcome, map the main parts and interactions, write the trade-off as two requirements that appear to conflict, generate separation or redesign options, choose a reversible check, and record which assumption or constraint changed.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: What contradiction did I expose, what separation or redesign did I check, and did it remove the conflict or only move it elsewhere?

faq.question: Is this a complete TRIZ method?
faq.answer: No. This is a practical TRIZ-inspired structuring exercise using contradiction and separation prompts. It does not represent the full TRIZ body of methods or claim a measured effect.
faq.answerHtml: No. This is a practical TRIZ-inspired structuring exercise using contradiction and separation prompts. It does not represent the full TRIZ body of methods or claim a measured effect.

intro.html: Some problems stay hard because the current design treats a trade-off as fixed. A TRIZ-inspired pass asks whether conflicting requirements can be separated or whether the system can be changed so they no longer compete in the same way.

sections.title: 1. State the unwanted result
sections.html: Describe what happens now and where it appears in the system. Separate symptoms from constraints you know are real.

sections.title: 2. Write the contradiction
sections.html: Express the conflict as two requirements: what must improve and what must not become worse. Add the condition under which each requirement matters.

sections.title: 3. Separate, redesign, and check
sections.html: Ask whether the requirements can be separated by time, place, condition, component, role, or state. Use a small reversible check and inspect side effects so the conflict is not merely moved elsewhere.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace pseudo-quantified TRIZ outcomes, fabricated pilots, arbitrary timing rules, and broad superiority claims with a bounded problem-structuring exercise inspired by contradiction and separation.
